tasks.title: Define the provider
Initialize Terraform
tasks.instructions:
Run `terraform init` in the terminal to download the Juju provider.

```bash
terraform init
```

You should see the provider being downloaded and installed.
hints: Make sure you are inside the lab working directory before running `terraform init`.

tasks.title: Create a Juju model
tasks.instructions:
Add a `juju_model` resource named "development" to `main.tf`:

```hcl
resource "juju_model" "development" {
  name = "development"
}
```

A model needs at minimum a `name`. You can optionally specify a cloud and region.
hints: If you omit cloud and region, Juju uses the controller's default cloud (LXD in our case).

tasks.title: Deploy the ubuntu charm
hints: `model_uuid` is a computed attribute on the `juju_model` resource, so you can reference it as `juju_model.development.uuid`.

tasks.title: Plan and apply
tasks.instructions:
Run `terraform plan` to see what will be created, then `terraform apply` to create the resources:

```bash
terraform plan
terraform apply -auto-approve
```
hints: `terraform plan` is read-only and shows the changes. `terraform apply -auto-approve` applies them without prompting.

tasks.title: Verify
tasks.instructions:
Verify your deployment with Juju:

```bash
juju status --model development
```

You should see the `ubuntu` application with 1 unit in `active` status.
hints: If the model name is different, replace `development` with your model name.

tasks.title: Clean up (optional)
tasks.instructions:
When you're done, destroy the resources:

```bash
terraform destroy -auto-approve
```
hints: This task is optional. It removes the model and application you created.
